item.title: reports: totals per account and currency
item.brief: Change the Python `reports` tool (reads CSV on stdin, prints per-account totals) to total per account and currency. Output header becomes `account,currency,total_cents`, rows sorted by account then currency. CSV without a currency column (old ledger output) still works and counts as USD. A malformed currency code in the input (not exactly three uppercase ASCII letters) prints an error to stderr and exits with status 2. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing, add tests for the per-currency totals, the USD fallback for old CSV, sort order, and the malformed-code exit, and update the README. Follow the shared contract exactly. Do not change the ledger repository.

item.title: ledger: currency column and currency validation
item.brief: Change the Rust `ledger` tool (stdin TSV to stdout CSV) for multiple currencies. Input lines may have a fourth column, the ISO 4217 currency code; when missing, the currency is USD. Output header becomes `date,account,amount_cents,currency` and every row gets its currency. A malformed currency code (not exactly three uppercase ASCII letters) prints an error naming the line number to stderr and exits with status 2; other input errors keep exiting with status 1. Keep `cargo test` passing, add tests for the default currency, an explicit currency, and a malformed code, and update the README. Follow the shared contract exactly. Do not change the reports repository.

pr.body:
Approach: Entry gains a currency field. parse_line accepts 3 or 4 tab-separated fields; a missing 4th field defaults to USD. parse_currency requires exactly three ASCII uppercase letters. ParseError distinguishes Input (exit 1) from Currency (exit 2); main maps the variant to the exit status and keeps the 'line N:' prefix on stderr.

Key files: src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, tests/ledger.rs (unit tests: default USD, explicit EUR, malformed codes, other input errors), tests/cli.rs (binary exit codes and line number on stderr), README.md.

Checks: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test (9 tests) all pass. Review: pass, no blocking findings.

Assumptions and limits: whitespace around the currency is trimmed, matching the other fields. An empty 4th column is a malformed currency (exit 2), not a missing one. Only the shape of the code is checked, not membership in the ISO 4217 list. Entry gained a public field, so struct-literal callers break. Crate version not bumped.
pr.summary: ledger: optional 4th TSV column sets currency (ISO 4217, default USD); output gains currency column. before: 3 columns, no currency. now: date,account,amount_cents,currency on every row; malformed currency exits 2, other input errors exit 1.
pr.title: ledger: add currency column and validate currency codes

agt_01M8GNG1886AQWZ1G5JHQ4P1PK:1.description: Currency is trimmed before validation, so ' EUR ' is accepted. The contract says exactly three A-Z letters and the README does not mention whitespace tolerance. This matches how date, account and amount are trimmed, so it is a decision to confirm or document, not a bug. at src/lib.rs:53

agt_01M8GNG1886AQWZ1G5JHQ4P1PK:2.description: An empty 4th column (trailing tab, e.g. '...\t1.00\t') is rejected with exit 2 as a bad currency, not treated as missing (USD). The contract's 'missing means USD' is ambiguous here. The behaviour is pinned by tests/ledger.rs:38 but not stated in the README. Lines of this shape previously exited 1. at src/lib.rs:53

agt_01M8GNG1886AQWZ1G5JHQ4P1PK:3.description: When a line has both a bad amount and a bad currency, the amount error wins and the exit is 1. A bad date with a bad currency also exits 1. The contract does not set precedence and the README does not document it. at src/lib.rs:51

agt_01M8GNG1886AQWZ1G5JHQ4P1PK:4.description: The README calls the currency an 'ISO 4217 code', which suggests membership checking. Only the shape (three uppercase ASCII letters) is validated, so codes like ZZZ are accepted. Consider saying 'shaped like an ISO 4217 code'. at README.md:14

agt_01M8GNG1886AQWZ1G5JHQ4P1PK:5.description: The author reported 11 passing tests. cargo test runs 9: 3 in tests/cli.rs and 6 in tests/ledger.rs. The code is fine, but the reported count is wrong. at tests/cli.rs:1

agt_01M8GNG1886AQWZ1G5JHQ4P1PK:6.description: The malformed-currency test has no non-ASCII case (for example 'ÉUR'), and nothing pins the whitespace-trimming behaviour. The implementation handles non-ASCII correctly (I probed 'ÉUR' and 'EUÉ': exit 2). Both are gaps worth a test. at tests/ledger.rs:38

agt_01M8GNG1886AQWZ1G5JHQ4P1PK:7.description: Entry gains a public currency field, which breaks any downstream struct-literal construction. Cargo.toml still says 0.3.0 despite the breaking CLI and API change. Nothing in the repo constructs Entry directly outside lib.rs. at src/lib.rs:10

agt_01M8GNG1886AQWZ1G5JHQ4P1PK:8.description: cargo fmt reflowed unrelated code (is_iso_date and the parse_cents whole-part parse) in the same commit. Behaviour is unchanged, but it adds diff noise to a functional change. at src/lib.rs:77

risk.why: Changes the CLI output header and row shape consumed by the reports tool, and adds a public field to Entry. Behaviour change, plus new tests. Review found no blocking issues and confirmed high.
